about.title: Placentia Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Placentia residents rely on nearby Orange County hospitals and clinics for everything from routine procedures to emergency care, and most of that care goes fine. But when a provider misses a diagnosis, makes a surgical error, or mishandles medication, the harm can be lasting. California treats these claims differently than a typical injury case — MICRA sets a shorter window to act, a mandatory 90-day notice before suing, and a cap on non-economic damages that shifts each year. A qualified medical expert almost always has to weigh in before a case can move forward, and a poor outcome by itself isn't proof of negligence. If you believe something went wrong with your care in Placentia, connecting with an attorney familiar with MICRA's specific requirements early on matters. LawProactive is a free service — we don't practice law, we simply connect you with an independent attorney so you can find out where you stand.

whyChoose.title: Why Timing and Process Matter in a MICRA Case

items.title: Short, Specific Deadlines
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from when you discover the harm, and never more than three years from the injury itself, to bring a claim. Missing that window can end a case regardless of merit.

items.title: 90-Day Notice Requirement
items.desc: Before a malpractice lawsuit can be filed, California law requires 90 days' advance notice to the provider. Handling this notice correctly and on time is part of building a case properly from the start.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Required
items.desc: A qualified medical expert typically must confirm that the care fell below the accepted standard. This is why a bad outcome alone isn't enough — the case has to show an actual departure from proper medical practice.

items.question: I live in Placentia — does it matter which hospital treated me?
items.answer: Not for whether MICRA applies; the same California rules on notice, deadlines, and damage caps apply no matter which Orange County facility was involved. What matters more is gathering your medical records and timeline as soon as possible. An attorney can help sort out the details once you're connected.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a medical malpractice claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have one year from when you discover (or reasonably should have discovered) the injury, but never more than three years from the date it happened. There's also a required 90-day notice period before filing suit. These deadlines are strict, so earlier action gives more options.

items.question: Is a bad medical outcome automatically malpractice?
items.answer: No — California law is clear that an unfavorable result by itself doesn't establish negligence. A claim generally needs a qualified medical expert to show the care fell below the accepted standard and caused harm. That's part of why early attorney involvement matters.
